battlefield.note: A ploughed field narrowing between Agincourt and Tramecourt woods, deep mud in the middle and the English line on a low rise with its stakes.

popup.title: Agincourt: The Muddy Field
popup.body:
You command King Henry V's small, tired army at the narrow end of a ploughed field between two woods. The rain has turned the field to mud: French knights and men-at-arms will be slow and clumsy in it. Keep your longbowmen on the low rise behind the stakes and shoot every wave as it struggles through the mud.

Objective: Hold Maisoncelle for 5:00.

On 25 October 1415 Henry V's outnumbered English army defeated the French at Agincourt. The French attacked across a muddy, narrowing field and were shot down by English archers before they reached the line.

popup.title: The French knights charge
popup.body: Mounted knights are charging from both wings to ride down your archers. The mud will slow them: shoot, and let the stakes do the rest.

popup.title: The vanguard advances
popup.body: The first French battle of dismounted men-at-arms is wading through the mud toward you.

popup.title: The second battle
popup.body: More French men-at-arms follow the first wave into the field.

popup.title: The baggage is raided
popup.body: French riders have slipped around Agincourt wood and are falling on the English baggage. Send help, but don't weaken the line.

popup.title: The last French charge
popup.body: The French rearguard makes a final mounted charge.
